report.headline: The $2,400 return dispute is rejected because the sofa was an accepted COM/custom final-sale item.
report.executive_summary: The dispute correctly identifies CHG-A01, a USD 2,400 charge for ORD-A01, an Alder three-seat sofa made with Customer's Own Material (COM). The return record shows an attempted customer-freight return that was refused, but the accepted Checkout Terms expressly state that COM pieces are final sale and cannot be returned or refunded. The Card Member's reliance on the general 30-day website statement is resolved by the adjacent custom-order exception and the accepted Checkout Terms. No credit is due.
report.detailed_reasoning:
CHG-A01 is directly disputed for USD 2,400 and links to CRD-A01, Hearth & Grain Furniture, and ORD-A01. ORD-A01 contains exactly one line item: one Alder three-seat sofa in the COM option at USD 2,400, so the full disputed amount is attributable to this purchase. The order was placed on 2026-07-02 and the charge posted for the same amount and date.

The allegation is RET because RTN-A01 records a customer-freight return attempt marked refused, with the sofa sent back to the Card Member. The record is undated and does not establish Merchant receipt, authorization, or a refund promise. Those evidentiary limitations do not change the result because the product was outside the applicable return entitlement.

LIN-A01 identifies COM as the selected option, and PRD-ALDER identifies COM and made-to-measure options as custom. ORD-A01 accepted POL-HGF-CO-V4 by checkbox at checkout before payment, and EVI-A01-1 records acceptance of version 4 at 14:03 on 2026-07-02. Clause CLS-HGF-CO-V4-4.3 states: "Any piece made in Customer's Own Material (COM) or made to measure is final sale and cannot be returned or refunded." The public Returns Page's general 30-day statement is expressly qualified by CLS-HGF-WEB-V4-2, which states that custom orders are final sale and refers to Checkout Terms 4.3. Thus, the apparent 30-day conflict is resolved by a specific, clear, disclosed, and accepted exception.

The Card Member correctly identifies the transaction and contests the Merchant's refusal, so this is not a misunderstanding-based not_a_dispute outcome. The Merchant's conduct was proper under the accepted terms, so the verdict is rejected rather than accepted or partially accepted. No refund or credit is linked to CHG-A01. The separate USD 2,400 refund for CHG-A02 belongs to a different date, Card, Card Member, order, and standard Oat linen sofa and cannot be applied here. No other-means payment is connected to this order.

charges.rationale: The charge is correctly identified and fully reconciled to ORD-A01's single USD 2,400 COM sofa. Although RTN-A01 records a refused return attempt, the accepted and unambiguous COM final-sale clause excludes the item from return and refund. Therefore no credit is due and the Card Member remains liable for the full disputed amount.

report.headline: $300 overcharge caused by an unauthorized Platinum Stays re-rating
report.executive_summary: The Card Member correctly identified CHG-B01 and disputes only $300 of its $1,300 amount. ORD-B01 was confirmed at $1,000 for two nights at $500 per night and was guaranteed with eligible Platinum Card CRD-B01. Harbor Point instead charged $1,300 after applying a $650-per-night rate because settlement used Gold Card CRD-B02. The merchant's records establish how the amount was calculated, but the cited folio condition was not accepted for this booking and conflicts with Amex Platinum Stays participation terms. The full $300 disputed amount should be credited.
report.detailed_reasoning:
DSP-2026-91002 is linked to CHG-B01 for exactly $300 of the $1,300 posted purchase. CHG-B01 is linked to ORD-B01, a two-night lodging booking with a confirmed total of $1,000 at $500 per night. The booking was under Platinum Stays and was guaranteed with active Platinum Card CRD-B01 ending 2002. The final charge was posted to active Gold Card CRD-B02 ending 2031, held by the same Card Member. That card substitution establishes the settlement instrument, not consent to a higher rate.

The merchant folio and Merchant Submission state that the stay was re-rated to $650 per night because the folio was settled with Gold. Two nights at $650 equals $1,300, so the merchant's calculation fully explains the posted amount and the $300 difference. However, the calculation does not establish that the re-rating was contractually authorized. ORD-B01 accepted Harbor Point Reservation Terms version 2 by booking confirmation. Clause CLS-HPH-RES-V2-1 states: 'The rate shown on the booking confirmation is the rate charged for the stay.' No accepted-policy edge connects ORD-B01 to the separate folio policy containing clause CLS-HPH-FOLIO-V1-7.

Even if the folio clause is read as clear in isolation, it conflicts with binding Amex terms. CLS-AMX-PS-PART-3.2 requires Harbor Point to honor the Platinum Stays rate confirmed at booking for a reservation made or guaranteed with an eligible Platinum Card. CLS-AMX-PS-PART-3.4 prohibits adding eligibility conditions in the merchant's reservation or folio terms. The booking guarantee with CRD-B01 satisfied the applicable eligibility condition. CLS-AMX-MR-4.6 also requires the lodging merchant to honor the confirmed reservation rate, and CLS-AMX-MR-4.4 directs that terms contradicting an Amex program be read against the merchant.

The charge is therefore an OVR dispute under the Amex Dispute Guide: the amount differs from what the Card Member agreed to pay, including re-rating. The merchant is responsible for the disputed excess. No refund, credit, other-means payment, duplicate charge, return, invoice, installment, or subscription path changes the result. The uncontested $1,000 booking amount is outside this decision.

charges.rationale: The confirmed booking total was $1,000, while the posted charge was $1,300. The merchant's folio shows two nights at $650, which accounts arithmetically for the $300 excess, but the re-rating was not authorized by the accepted reservation terms or applicable Amex program terms. The disputed amount is limited to $300; the Card Member remains liable for the uncontested $1,000.

report.headline: Harbor Point overcharged $300 by re-rating a confirmed Platinum Stays booking
report.executive_summary: The dispute concerns a $300 portion of the $1,300 charge CHG-B01. ORD-B01 was confirmed at $1,000—two nights at $500 per night—and was guaranteed with eligible Platinum Card CRD-B01 ending 2002. Harbor Point instead charged $1,300 after settling the folio on Gold Card CRD-B02 ending 2031 and applying a $650 nightly rate. The confirmed booking rate governed, and the merchant's settlement-card re-rating condition was both unaccepted for this order and inconsistent with applicable Amex participation terms. Harbor Point owes the full disputed $300.
report.detailed_reasoning:
This is an amount-differs-from-agreement dispute because the Card Member correctly identified the lodging charge and contests the $300 difference between the confirmed $1,000 booking and the $1,300 posted charge. The charge is directly linked to ORD-B01 and MER-HPH. The booking record and EVI-B01-2 establish two nights at the Platinum Stays rate of $500 per night, for a total of $1,000, guaranteed with Platinum Card CRD-B01 ending 2002. Reservation Terms version 2 was accepted by booking confirmation, and Clause 1 states: "The rate shown on the booking confirmation is the rate charged for the stay."

The merchant's folio and submission establish how the excess arose: two nights were re-rated to $650 per night and settled with Gold Card CRD-B02 ending 2031, producing $1,300. The arithmetic is reconciled: $1,300 charged minus $1,000 confirmed equals the $300 disputed amount. No linked refund, credit, other-means payment, or separate charge reduces the disputed amount.

Harbor Point's cited Folio Terms Clause 7 says the Platinum Stays rate applies only when the folio is settled with an American Express Platinum Card and otherwise permits re-rating. That clause was not shown accepted for ORD-B01. More importantly, it conflicts with accepted Reservation Terms Clause 1 and with applicable Amex terms. Harbor Point participates in Platinum Stays, ORD-B01 was under that program, and the reservation was made or guaranteed with an eligible Platinum Card. Amex Clause 3.2 requires the participating property to honor the confirmed rate for such a reservation; Clause 3.4 prohibits added eligibility conditions in the merchant's reservation or folio terms; and Merchant Regulations Clause 4.6 requires the confirmed lodging rate to be honored. Under Merchant Regulations Clause 4.4, the conflicting merchant term is read against the merchant.

The fact that CRD-B02 was charged rather than CRD-B01 does not defeat the confirmed-rate entitlement. Both cards belong to the same Card Member, but the graph does not establish why the charged card differed from the guarantee card. That unresolved routing cause is immaterial to the merchant's liability because the merchant's own records identify Gold settlement as the reason for the prohibited re-rating. The appropriate result is a $300 credit and no Card Member liability.

charges.rationale: The $1,300 charge is linked to the $1,000 confirmed booking. The $300 excess resulted from Harbor Point's re-rating from $500 to $650 per night after settlement with Gold. The accepted booking terms and applicable Amex terms required honoring the confirmed Platinum Stays rate, and the merchant's contrary folio condition was not accepted for this order and conflicts with those rules.

report.executive_summary: The Card Member correctly identified the $540 Northwind purchase and disputed only $100. Northwind charged the agreed listed price of $540 ($390 parka plus $150 boots), and the $100 benefit was an Amex-funded statement credit rather than a Merchant discount. Ordinary Offer eligibility failed because the Offer was enrolled on Platinum Card CRD-C01, while the purchase was charged to Gold Card CRD-C02. However, the purchase otherwise met the tested Offer conditions, both Cards belonged to the same Card Member, and no prior Offer goodwill was found. Under the Amex Dispute Guide, a $100 Amex-funded goodwill credit is granted. No Merchant refund is due.
report.detailed_reasoning:
The allegation concerns an amount/discount not applied, so the category is OVR regardless of outcome. CHG-C01 is a posted $540 Northwind Outfitters purchase for ORD-C01, and the dispute challenges exactly $100. The order and invoice reconcile to one $390 storm parka and one $150 pair of trail boots, totaling $540. The accepted Northwind terms state that items are charged at listed price and that issuer Offers are administered by the issuer, not Northwind. The Merchant submission and invoice confirm that no Northwind promotion or promo code applied.

OFR-NWO-100 is an Amex-funded $100 credit with a $500 threshold at Northwind. It was enrolled on CRD-C01, Platinum ending 3003, while CHG-C01 was charged to CRD-C02, Gold ending 3017. Although both Cards belong to CMB-C01, CLS-AMX-OFFER-1 requires enrollment and payment on the same specific Card. The purchase was direct from the named Merchant and exceeded the $500 threshold in a single $540 transaction; no excluded-goods, intermediary-purchase, return, duplicate, or Merchant-refund issue is established. Ordinary Offer eligibility therefore failed only on the specific-Card condition.

The missing $100 does not make Northwind liable. CLS-AMX-OFFER-3 assigns Offer funding and statement-credit posting to Amex and says the Merchant charges its normal price. The charged amount therefore remains $540, with $100 disputed and $440 Card Member liability if no credit were awarded. Applying the written goodwill clauses, the Offer was enrolled on another Card held by the same Card Member, the purchase otherwise met the Offer terms, and the only verified prior resolved dispute was rejected and was not an Offer-goodwill credit. The stated conditions for one goodwill credit are satisfied, so the $100 credit is granted as an Amex-funded goodwill credit, not as a Merchant refund.

charges.rationale: The $540 charge was correctly billed at the agreed listed price, so Northwind owes no refund. The $100 Amex Offer was enrolled on a different Card from the Card used for payment, defeating ordinary eligibility. The purchase otherwise met the direct-Merchant and $500 single-transaction conditions; both Cards belonged to the same Card Member; and no earlier Offer goodwill was found. The Amex Dispute Guide therefore supports and, under the adjudication rule, requires the one-time $100 goodwill credit.

report.executive_summary: The Card Member correctly identified the $540 Northwind purchase and disputed $100, but Northwind did not overcharge them. The order and invoice total $540 ($390 parka plus $150 boots), and the Merchant charged that agreed amount. The $100 benefit was funded and posted by Amex, not Northwind. The Offer was enrolled on CRD-C01 but the purchase was charged to the Card Member's different Card, CRD-C02, so the ordinary Offer credit was not contractually due. However, the conditions for the one-time Amex Offer goodwill credit are satisfied: both Cards belong to the same Card Member, the purchase otherwise met the Offer conditions, and no prior Offer goodwill is recorded. Grant a $100 Amex-funded goodwill credit; Merchant liability is $0 and Card Member liability for the disputed portion is $0.
report.detailed_reasoning:
The disputed charge is correctly identified as CHG-C01: a posted $540 USD purchase for ORD-C01 at Northwind Outfitters, charged to CRD-C02. The disputed amount is $100, not the full $540. ORD-C01 contains a $390 Storm parka and $150 Trail boots, and the invoice confirms "$390 + $150 = $540" with no promo code. Thus the posted charge equals the agreed and listed-price total.

The allegation is classified as OVR because the Card Member alleges that an expected $100 discount or credit was not applied. The evidence does not establish a Merchant overcharge. The accepted Northwind sale terms state that listed prices apply and that issuer Offers are administered by the issuer. CLS-AMX-OFFER-3 likewise states that Amex funds and posts the Offer credit while the Merchant charges its normal price and is not responsible for the credit.

OFR-NWO-100 was a $100 Amex-funded Offer requiring a single $500-or-more purchase at Northwind. The transaction was direct and totaled $540, so the Merchant, spend, and single-transaction conditions were met. However, the Offer was enrolled on CRD-C01, Platinum ending 3003, while CHG-C01 was charged to CRD-C02, Gold ending 3017. CLS-AMX-OFFER-1 requires enrollment and payment on the same specific Card and excludes use of another Card, even when both Cards are held by the same Card Member. Therefore, the ordinary Offer credit was not earned on CHG-C01. No connected fulfillment, statement-credit, reversal, refund, or alternate-payment record exists; unrelated background credits cannot be attributed to this charge.

The goodwill exception applies. CLS-AMX-DG-G-2 permits one Amex-funded Offer goodwill credit when the Offer was enrolled on another Card held by the same Card Member, the purchase otherwise met the Offer terms, and the Card Member has no earlier Offer goodwill. CRD-C01 and CRD-C02 are both connected to CMB-C01. The only linked prior resolved dispute for CMB-C01 was rejected and was not an Offer goodwill matter. A same-name dispute belonging to CMB-C02 is a look-alike and is excluded based on Card Member identity. Under CLS-AMX-DG-V-1, the appropriate result is goodwill_credit because Northwind is not at fault and Amex funds the credit.

The $100 reconciliation is: $100 Amex goodwill credit + $0 Card Member liability = $100 disputed amount. The remaining $440 of the $540 charge is outside the dispute and remains valid. There is no Merchant credit or Merchant liability.

CLS-AMX-OFFER-1 requires payment with the same specific Card and expressly says an Offer on one Card does not apply to another Card, even when both Cards are held by the same Card Member. Because CHG-C01 was charged to CRD-C02, the ordinary Offer credit was not earned automatically. CLS-AMX-OFFER-3 assigns funding and posting of the credit to Amex, not Northwind, and the accepted Northwind issuer-Offer clause is consistent with that allocation.

CLS-AMX-DG-G-2 specifically addresses an Offer enrolled on another Card held by the same Card Member and permits one goodwill credit when the purchase otherwise met the Offer terms. report.detailed_reasoning:
The dispute challenges exactly three recurring postings: CHG-E02 dated 2026-06-12, CHG-E03 dated 2026-07-12, and CHG-E04 dated 2026-08-12. Each charge directly links to StreamCo, descriptor SC*DIGITAL SVCS, and the same active monthly Family subscription SUB-E02. Each also posted to Additional Card CRD-E02 ending 5013, the card linked to SUB-E02. The Basic Card Member is responsible for Additional Card charges on the same account.

The May 4 email says, "Your StreamCo Individual plan has been cancelled. You won't be charged again for this plan." The communication asserts SUB-E01, the USD 12.99 Individual plan billed to Basic Card 5005. It does not identify SUB-E02, the USD 22.99 Family plan billed to Card 5013. StreamCo Terms v3 were accepted for SUB-E02 by checkbox at sign-up. Clause 5 states that each plan is a separate subscription and cancelling one plan does not cancel another. Clauses 2 and 4 provide for monthly renewal until cancellation and billing through the end of the current period after cancellation. Merchant evidence states that the Family plan remained active and had never been cancelled; usage evidence records four profiles streaming on 41 days since June.

The same descriptor is used across multiple StreamCo subscriptions, so the descriptor alone is not treated as unique. The relevant charge paths nonetheless consistently identify SUB-E02 and Card 5013. Other StreamCo charges, including a separate Family subscription on Card 1961 and the refunded Individual charge on Card 5005, are look-alikes and are not part of this dispute.

There is no refund, reversal, negative credit, or other-means payment linked to the three disputed charges. The separate USD 12.99 refund concerns CHG-E01 and the cancelled Individual plan, not these charges. The missing explicit Family enrollment timestamp and Product/Order path are documentary limitations, but no record contradicts the active subscription, accepted terms, direct charge-to-subscription links, card linkage, or usage evidence. They therefore do not change the outcome and do not constitute a system improvement.

Under the Amex Dispute Guide, this is CNR because the allegation concerns cancelled recurring billing. Under the verdict standard, the charges were not caused by Merchant error; the claim rests on confusing two different plans and Cards. The appropriate result is not_a_dispute, with no credit.

report.detailed_reasoning:
The allegation is recurring billing after cancellation, so the category is CNR. The statement descriptor SC*DIGITAL SVCS resolves to StreamCo, and the charge records, card records, and subscription records consistently identify the disputed transactions. CHG-E02, CHG-E03, and CHG-E04 are each $22.99, dated June 12, July 12, and August 12, and each links directly to active monthly Family subscription SUB-E02. The accepted StreamCo Subscription Terms version 3 authorize monthly renewal until cancellation, provide cancellation through Account > Plans, and state that each plan is separate. Each charge was billed to active Family subscription SUB-E02 and Additional Card CRD-E02 ending 5013. The May 4 cancellation confirmation was authentic, but it cancelled only SUB-E01, the separate USD 12.99 Individual plan billed to Card ending 5005. report.detailed_reasoning:
The allegation is recurring-billing continuity/cancellation, so the category is CNR. The three disputed charges are CHG-E02, CHG-E03, and CHG-E04, posted on June 12, July 12, and August 12, 2026. They share the StreamCo merchant and descriptor SC*DIGITAL SVCS, each is USD 22.99, and each is linked to active Family subscription SUB-E02 and CRD-E02 ending 5013. The three disputed portions total exactly USD 68.97.

COM-E01 is a genuine StreamCo cancellation confirmation dated May 4, but its text says only: “Your StreamCo Individual plan has been cancelled. You won't be charged again for this plan.” The communication is linked to SUB-E01, the cancelled Individual plan billed to Card ending 5005. It does not identify SUB-E02 or Card ending 5013. The accepted StreamCo terms provide that plans renew monthly until cancelled, cancellation takes effect for billing at the end of the current period, and each plan is a separate subscription; cancelling one plan does not cancel another. SUB-E02 was accepted by checkbox under the applicable version of those terms, remained active, and merchant usage evidence records four profiles streaming on 41 days since June.

The Additional Card relationship does not invalidate the charges. CRD-E02 is an active Additional Card on the open account ACC-E01, and the Basic Card Member who filed the dispute is responsible for Additional Card charges under CMA 5.1. The CNR evidence rule requires the cancellation record to be matched to the plan and Card billed. That match fails here because the cancellation concerns SUB-E01/Card 5005 while the disputed charges concern SUB-E02/Card 5013. Under the outcome rule, these are correctly billed charges for a different plan from the one the Card Member believed was cancelled, so the result is not_a_dispute rather than rejected.

The same-descriptor background charges CHG-BG-2884 through CHG-BG-2887 were ruled out: although they are also USD 22.99 StreamCo Family charges, they belong to Card ending 1961, subscription SUB-BG-0017, a different account and a separate dispute. The separate USD 12.99 refund CHG-E01R applies to CHG-E01 for the Individual plan and does not credit any disputed charge. No duplicate presentment, other-means payment, replacement/token mismatch, or relevant prior dispute is connected to this case.

The Case Notebook conflict is factual, not textual: the Card Member read the Individual cancellation as cancelling all StreamCo plans. The cited Merchant and Amex clauses are clear and consistent. The Notebook's improvement idea is retained as a process improvement only: cancellation confirmation should identify the cancelled plan and clearly show any other plan and Card that remain active. No Amex policy, merchant-policy, data, or evidentiary gap caused the outcome.
